That said, I'm not claiming remote work is universally perfect. Some people genuinely thrive on in-person energy, and some kinds of work — early-stage team building, hands-on mentorship — do suffer without physical presence. Nuance and honesty aren't the same thing as watering down a position. If you disagree with my read, I'd genuinely like to hear why — maybe you've seen something I haven't. But "both sides have merits" as a reflex isn't balance, it's just avoidance.
